newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends lower but off session troughs.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends lower but off session troughs.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended lower but off its session troughs after an active Friday session, the currency being aided in part by strength in the Australian dollar.
Kiwi finished at US$0.6975/82 from 0.6992/99 at the opening and lost ground on the Trade-Weighted Index to 68.47 from 68.72, but the currency was off its session low of 0.6962.
"Really the main reason for the Kiwi's strength today is the fact that the Aussie is so well-bid," said one dealer.
"So the market is very short Aussie and to a certain extent the interbank market is short Kiwi as well," he said.
Most commentators expect the Kiwi to move lower after Thursday's easing of conditions by the Reserve Bank.
"My expectation is that we will see it down towards its lows. It won't break through 0.7000 again and we anticipate next week that it will go lower than it is today, he said.
